data.title: X Financial Flat on Release of Q3 Numbers
data.description:
X Financial , a leading Chinese fintech platform, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Total net revenue in Q3 2026 was RMB771.5 million (US$115.1 million), a decrease of 60.7% year-over-year and 22.4% quarter-over-quarter.

The year-over-year decline was mainly attributable to substantially lower loan facilitation volumes, which reduced loan facilitation service revenue and post-origination service revenue, as well as lower financing income.

Total loan amount facilitated and originated in Q3 2026 was RMB4.35 billion, down 62.6% quarter-over-quarter and down 87.1% year-over-year.

Net loss in Q3 2026 was RMB159.6 million (US$23.8 million), compared with net income of RMB421.2 million a year ago and RMB47.0 million in Q2 2026, primarily reflecting income tax expense of RMB184.6 million and a loss from equity in affiliates, net of tax, of RMB70.9 million, which together exceeded income before income taxes of RMB101.9 million.

Delinquency rates for loans 31-60 days past due increased to 2.40% (from 1.73% at the end of Q2 2026 and 1.85% a year ago); loans 91-180 days past due declined to 7.83% (from 9.09% at the end of Q2 2026, though up from 3.52% a year ago).

During the quarter, the Company observed an increase in the 31-60 day delinquency rate, which may continue in the near term. The Company believes these trends are consistent with broader industry patterns.

XYF shares gathered four cents, or 0.8%, to $5.24.

Save as expressly provided in the Amended Consent Solicitation Memorandum, capitalised terms that are used in this section shall have the same meanings given to them in the relevant Conditions or the applicable Supplemental Trust Deed (as applicable).

  • Condition 3.5 (Asset Sales) is amended to further restrict the ability of the Parent and its Subsidiaries to consummate an Asset Sale for the duration of the Additional Conditions Period without obtaining an opinion from an independent financial adviser as to the fair market value assessment; and
  • a new Condition 3.15 (Additional Financing Undertakings) is included as a new undertaking requiring the Parent and its Subsidiaries not to, for the duration of the Additional Conditions Period:

(x) make any payment under any shareholder loan advanced by a shareholder of the Parent or any Affiliate thereof (other than a Subsidiary) or any Permitted Holder to the Parent or any Subsidiary (each, a "Shareholder Loan") other than a repayment of principal on its scheduled maturity either funded solely through (1) a new Shareholder Loan contractually subordinated to the Notes in connection with any Refinancing or (2) a substantially concurrent issuance of Capital Stock (other than Disqualified Stock) of the Parent; or

(y) repay, prepay or redeem any indebtedness for borrowed monies and any indebtedness evidenced by bonds, notes, debentures or similar instruments (excluding Shareholder Loans) before its scheduled maturity, other than in connection with a refinancing of such indebtedness no more than two months prior to its scheduled maturity;

which, in each case, are for the benefit of Noteholders and shall apply for the duration of the Additional Conditions Period (as defined below) in respect of a Series of Notes (such additional conditions, in respect of a Series of Notes, the "Additional Conditions").

data.title: 3,269 Bitcoin moves from Coinbase Institutional to an unknown wallet
data.description:
A wallet has moved 3,269 BTC out of Coinbase Institutional and into a brand-new address with no public label, according to blockchain tracker Whale Alert.

The transfer is part of a recurring pattern. Whale Alert has logged a series of hefty outflows from Coinbase Institutional wallets, and traders often read the size and structure of those moves as clues about institutional sentiment toward Bitcoin.

The transaction moved 3,269 BTC from a Coinbase Institutional hot wallet to an address that had not been identified before. A hot wallet is one connected to the internet.

Whale Alert recorded several other Coinbase Institutional outflows during November, many of them above 800 BTC.

Among the flagged transfers were 833 BTC, worth approximately $51 million, and 889 BTC, worth approximately $54 million. Another moved 872 BTC, valued at approximately $51 million.

The largest comparable move on record in the research was 2,082 BTC, worth approximately $130 million. The latest 3,269 BTC transfer is larger than all of them.

No public report has matched another transaction to this exact amount.

Fresh addresses are frequently used to protect client privacy. If every large holder reused the same public address, anyone with a block explorer could track their entire position.

The likely explanations for these flows include client withdrawals, custody rotations, and privacy-oriented shuffling of coins between addresses.

There is also a boomerang effect. Some of the addresses receiving these Coinbase outflows have cycled back to Coinbase wallets within days.

None of these transactions has been publicly linked to a direct sale of assets. Bitcoin moving off an exchange is not the same as Bitcoin being sold.

During the comparable transfers in late November, Bitcoin traded in a range of around $59,000 to $61,000.

Coinbase Institutional's clients are funds, corporations, and other large holders that want professional custody for their crypto. Its wallets hold assets on behalf of those clients, which separates their activity from Coinbase's own corporate holdings.

When coins leave a Coinbase Institutional wallet, it is usually a client moving its own money, not Coinbase making a bet.

A 3,269 BTC transfer to an unknown wallet could reflect a client pulling assets into self-custody, a fund reorganizing its storage setup, or simple address rotation.

If the receiving address later sends coins to a trading venue, that would change the picture considerably. Deposits onto exchanges are traditionally the more meaningful tell for potential selling. Withdrawals into fresh wallets lean the other way, though not with certainty.

A steady stream of large Coinbase Institutional outflows, several above 800 BTC and now one at 3,269 BTC, points to sustained institutional activity on the custody side of the market.

data.title: Germany's Schwarz Digits bets on flexible cloud to challenge Big Tech
data.description:
German cloud provider Schwarz Digits designed its platform to allow customers to easily switch providers, said its chief executive, arguing that firms are increasingly seeking alternatives to becoming locked into a single tech ecosystem.

The company, part of the Schwarz Group that also owns retailer Lidl, offers cloud services on a pay-as-you-go basis without long-term commitments, CEO Christian Mueller said on Thursday.

"We're trying to bring the simplicity of retail into the IT world," said Mueller.

Schwarz Digits is seeking to position itself as a European alternative to major cloud providers as policymakers and businesses look to reduce dependence on US technology giants.

Mueller said digital sovereignty starts with "freedom of choice" and the ability to switch providers without disrupting operations.

He contrasted Schwarz Digits' approach with cloud services that he said can create vendor lock-in.

"There are services that create lock-in. The service you've built around only exists in that provider's proprietary environment," he said. "Technically, you can't leave on your own terms. That's exactly what we're trying to avoid."

Mueller said such flexibility was becoming more important as companies adopt artificial intelligence and rely on technologies outside their direct control.

data.title: Southwest Airlines Offers Rapid Rewards Members Promotional Companion Pass
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - On Friday, Southwest Airlines (LUV) announced that it is offering Rapid Rewards members a promotional Companion Pass after completing one qualifying round-trip flight or two one-way flights between November 27, 2026, and January 5, 2027.

Southwest's Companion Pass allows Rapid Rewards members to designate one person to fly with them free on qualifying flights.

To earn the promotional pass, members must register and book one qualifying round-trip flight or two one-way flights between November 27 and 29, 2026, complete the travel by January 5, 2027, and use the pass for a designated companion between January 8 and March 3, 2027.

Additionally, members who apply for a Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card by December 14, 2026, get approved and meet the welcome bonus spending requirements can use those bonus points toward a Companion Pass valid through December 31, 2027.

On the NYSE, the shares were trading 0.78 percent up at $46.31.

  • Exports of goods rise 3.2% to $215.8 billion
  • Wholesale, retail inventories soar amid robust domestic demand

By Lucia Mutikani

The US trade deficit in goods widened sharply in October as an AI infrastructure buildout boosted imports to a record high, potentially putting trade on course to again subtract from economic growth in the fourth quarter.

The surge in imports reported by the Commerce Department on Friday was also across other categories, including motor vehicles, industrial supplies and consumer goods, reflecting robust domestic demand. Imports have increased at a rapid clip despite President Donald Trump's aggressive tariffs.

Trump has defended the duties as necessary to shrink the trade gap and rejuvenate the nation's industrial base. The Trump administration this week proposed new maximum potential rates of 20% to 40% on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan ​and the European Union, to counter what the White House said was excess industrial capacity that these countries are promoting.

"The trade deficit in goods worsened in October, which will take a toll on economic growth in the fourth quarter," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "Capital goods imports are surging, showing that AI doesn't always lead to greater US economic growth."

The goods trade shortfall jumped 10.7%, or $14.4 billion, to $149.5 billion last month, the highest level since March 2025, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the goods deficit at $133 billion.

Goods imports shot up 6.1%, or $21.1 billion, to $365.3 billion, the highest level since the government started tracking the series in 1992. The broad increase in imports was led by capital goods, which soared 8.5%. Capital goods increased 80.0% on a year-on-year basis in October.

Businesses are aggressively spending on AI, giving the technology a prominent role in the economy. But the AI infrastructure buildout is heavily reliant on imports, which are a subtraction from gross domestic product growth.

Imports of consumer goods advanced 2.6% while those of other goods increased 4.5%. Domestic demand, which includes business investment and consumer spending, grew in the third quarter at its fastest pace in more than five years.

Imports of industrial supplies, which include crude oil and nonmonetary gold, increased 6.0% last month, while those of motor vehicles, engines and parts accelerated 4.1%. Imports of foods, feeds and beverages rose 2.5%.

AI ADDING LESS TO GDP GROWTH

"This year's surge in capital goods imports is one reason why AI is adding less to GDP than corporate spending figures suggest," economists at Goldman Sachs wrote in a note.

Exports of goods increased 3.2%, or $6.7 billion, to $215.8 billion. Exports of industrial supplies advanced 4.9% and shipments of capital goods rose 3.4%.

Exports of motor vehicles, engines and parts vaulted 5.7%, while those of consumer goods increased 4.2%. But exports of foods, feeds and beverages slumped 7.9%.

The government reported on Wednesday that trade sliced off 3.21 percentage points from GDP growth in the third quarter. The drag was, however, more than offset by robust growth in consumer spending and business investment in equipment, mostly AI-related. The economy grew at a 4.3% annualized rate last quarter after expanding at a 2.2% pace in the April-June period.

Trade has not contributed to gross domestic product growth for four straight quarters, reflecting strong domestic demand.

The anticipated hit to GDP growth from trade this quarter could be blunted by businesses rebuilding inventories to meet demand.

The Census Bureau also reported on Friday that wholesale inventories increased 0.9% in October after rising 0.8% in September. Stocks at wholesalers were lifted by a 1.6% jump in durable goods inventories. Retail inventories increased 0.8% after climbing 0.7% in September. Stocks at motor vehicle and parts dealers jumped 1.3% after rising 0.6% in September.

Excluding motor vehicles and parts, retail inventories increased 0.6% last month after gaining 0.7% in September. This component goes into the calculation of GDP.

Inventory investment rebounded in the third quarter after declining for five straight quarters. It added 1.64 percentage points to GDP growth last quarter.

Economists at Goldman Sachs lowered their fourth-quarter GDP growth estimate by 0.2 percentage point to a 2.2% rate. This estimate also factored in October's wholesale and inventory data, which they said partly offset the drag from the large trade deficit.

data.title: CDC confirms ninth measles-linked death for 2026 as case count tops 6,000
data.description:
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed nine mortalities linked to measles in the U.S. this year, as the case count attributed to the vaccine-preventable disease exceeded 6,000 to reach the highest in over three decades.

Updating its measles case numbers on Wednesday, the agency said that the U.S. has recorded 43 new outbreaks this year compared with 48 and 16 in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

97% of the 6,039 measles  cases detected this year have been associated with those outbreaks compared with 90% in 2025 when the confirmed case numbers reached 2,289, surpassing the previous highest case count of 2,126 recorded in 1992.

However, the CDC’s official death toll trails the publicly available data from state health departments, which indicate at least 14 measles-linked deaths this year: nine in Pennsylvania, three in Wisconsin, and one each in Virginia and New York state.

The discrepancy arose after the U.S. Health and Human Services Department, under which the CDC operates, decided to abandon state-tallied data and instead use official death records tracked by the National Center for Health Statistics to confirm measles-associated deaths.

Noting that only 4% of cases were detected in individuals who received at least one dose of the MMR vaccine that prevents measles, the CDC said that the live-attenuated shot, which also targets mumps and rubella, remains safe and effective.

BofA Research also sees a potential pick-up in residential real estate transactions in 2027 as a possible catalyst for big-ticket spending, following a prolonged period without a meaningful housing cycle since the COVID-19 pandemic.

The shift in sector positioning comes as the U.S. enters the holiday shopping season, with Black Friday taking place today.

data.title: Hindalco Appoints Hemant Sikka As Deputy MD, Reappoints Satish Pai For 2028
data.description:
Sikka will join as Deputy Managing Director from January 4, 2027, with responsibility for Hindalco's India business transitioning to him in phases

Hindalco Industries has appointed Hemant Sikka as Deputy Managing Director and Key Managerial Personnel (KMP), effective January 4, 2027. The company has also reappointed Satish Pai as Managing Director for another year, from January 1 to December 31, 2028, as it prepares for a phased transition of its India business leadership.

The appointments were approved by Hindalco's board at a meeting held on November 23, 2026, following recommendations from the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.

Sikka will work closely with Pai and the company's leadership team, with responsibilities for the India business transitioning to him progressively. The company said the transition would be implemented in phases to ensure business continuity and organisational effectiveness.

Sikka Joins From Mahindra Logistics

Sikka joins Hindalco from the Mahindra Group, where he currently serves as Managing Director and CEO of Mahindra Logistics. He is also a member of the Mahindra and Mahindra Group Executive Board.

He brings more than three decades of experience across manufacturing, operations, procurement and business leadership.

During his tenure at Mahindra, Sikka held several leadership positions, including Chief Purchase Officer of the Automotive and Farm Sector and Head of Manufacturing for the Automotive division. He also gained international experience with SsangYong Motors in South Korea.

Before joining the Mahindra Group in 2000, he spent nine years at Maruti Suzuki.

Sikka holds a BTech degree from NIT Kurukshetra and an MBA from the Faculty of Management Studies (FMS), Delhi.

Satish Pai To Continue As Managing Director

Pai has been Managing Director of Hindalco since August 2016 and also oversees the operations of its subsidiary, Novelis Inc.

During his tenure, the company has focused on moving beyond its traditional metals commodity business towards value-added solutions in aluminium and copper.

According to Hindalco, the company has been ranked the world's most sustainable aluminium company in the Dow Jones Sustainability Indices for four consecutive years since 2020.

Pai holds a mechanical engineering degree from IIT Madras. He received an honorary doctorate from Utkal University in 2024 and was named Fortune India's Best CEO in the Mining and Metals category in 2025.

data.title: Dan Ives Calls Nvidia's China Risk 'Containable', While Gene Munster Says AI Trade Is In The 'Penalty Box'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ives stated that he's still bullish on AI even if 20% of data centers never get built, and financing falls 25%.
  • He called China and the "Asia loophole" a "containable 15% to 20% of revenue at most" for Nvidia.
  • Deepwater's Gene Munster bought Nvidia after Huang's ouster and said the AI trade is "still in the penalty box."

Two of Wall Street's prominent Nvidia (NVDA) bulls, Dan Ives and Gene Munster, are sticking with their AI investment thesis despite market volatility.

Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director Dan Ives said on Friday that the firm recently stress-tested its AI outlook under several adverse scenarios, including a slowdown in data center construction, tighter chip exports to Asia and reduced financing, and still came away bullish.

Meanwhile, Deepwater Asset Management managing partner Gene Munster also backed Nvidia on Friday, revealing in an interview with CNBC that he bought shares after Huang's departure and before the CEO's reinstatement.

NVDA stock fell 1.8% in morning trade on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the AI bellwether trended in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day.

Dan Ives Says Nvidia's China Risk Remains 'Containable'

"Our stress test stands: assume 20% of the data centers do not get built, the Asia loophole revenue is shut off, and financing is curtailed by 25%, and we are still bullish on the AI thesis into the next two to three years," Ives wrote on X on Friday.

The reference to the "Asia loophole" concerns Nvidia chips reaching China through third-party countries in the region. The issue drew renewed attention after Bloomberg reported that one of Nvidia's most powerful Blackwell server racks had surfaced at a data center in Shanghai.

"We continue to expect a rollercoaster ride ahead, but our thesis in the AI Revolution buildout and the winners (including Nvidia) have not changed," Ives wrote. According to him, China and the associated export loophole "remain a containable 15% to 20% of revenue.”

Ives also pointed to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's upcoming meetings in Washington, saying Huang "carries the weight of the entire tech sector and AI Revolution thesis when he marches into DC" next week, "as the politicians are eagerly awaiting these sessions with all the world watching."

Gene Munster Is Buying Nvidia, But Says Investor Psychology Is Lagging

"I've been buying Nvidia. I bought it after Jensen left. Stock was higher at that point, and the mistake I made was focusing just on the fundamentals," Munster told CNBC. "There's obviously the psychological piece, and this is the maddening part."

Munster said Nvidia's business outlook remained strong, pointing to growth expectations that continue to exceed Wall Street estimates. He noted that Nvidia's projected growth for calendar 2027 stood at 75%, compared with the Street's 70% estimate.

"So the fundamentals, I think, are in great shape. I think we're still sub 1% in terms of the adoption," Munster said, referring to the early stage of AI adoption. "The AI trade is largely still in the penalty box. I think that the substance of the fundamentals will eventually impact the psychology and then move it higher.”

Munster declined to call a market bottom but said investors willing to hold AI-related stocks through the current volatility could be rewarded over the next year.

The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained more than 1% on Friday morning, tracking a broad Nasdaq-100 rally, even as Nvidia, Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) and CoreWeave (CRWV) led losses. Retail sentiment around the ETF on Stocktwits slipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ over the past day.

data.title: Skydance Plans To Pay Down Debt Due In 2027, Ends $4B Financing Facility After Warner Bros. Discovery Deal
data.description:
Key points:
  • The planned redemptions cover all of Skydance's 2027 debt maturities that can currently be redeemed at par.
  • About $168 million of 3.755% notes will remain, which Skydance expects to repay at or before their March 15, 2027 maturity.
  • Skydance registered up to 4.62 billion Class B shares for potential resale by certain stockholders.

Skydance Corporation (SKYD) disclosed Friday that it had terminated a $4 billion receivables securitization facility and issued notices to redeem approximately $709.5 million in notes maturing in 2027, following its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

The company has repaid and closed a $3.9 billion financing arrangement backed by money owed to its businesses. It is also paying off three bonds due in 2027 early, at full value plus interest, leaving about $168 million of 2027 debt it expects to repay by March.

Skydance said in its November 27 filing that the steps are in line with its previously announced capital plan and part of a wider push to cut debt.

Skydance Details Debt Redemption Plans

On November 20, Warner Bros. Discovery Receivables Funding, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Skydance, repaid all amounts due under its receivables purchase agreement and terminated the facility.

The $4 billion securitization facility related to amounts owed by third parties to affiliates of Warner Bros. Discovery Receivables Funding. Approximately $3.9 billion had been outstanding.

Separately, Skydance subsidiaries issued notices on November 25 for the full redemption of three series of notes maturing in 2027:

  • Paramount Global's 2.90% senior notes: approximately $584.3 million.
  • Warner Media, LLC's 3.80% notes: approximately $33.4 million.
  • Discovery Communications, LLC's 1.90% senior notes: approximately €84.3 million ($91.9 million).

The dollar-denominated notes are scheduled for redemption on December 23, while the euro-denominated notes are scheduled for December 29. The redemption price is 100% of principal, plus accrued and unpaid interest up to, but excluding, the applicable redemption date.

What Debt Remains?

Skydance said the planned redemptions would address all its 2027 debt maturities currently eligible for redemption at par. After those redemptions, approximately $168 million in Discovery Global Holdings' 3.755% notes would remain outstanding.

Those notes are not currently callable at par. The company expects to repay them at or before their March 15, 2027 maturity.

Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 6, 2026. As part of the transaction's equity financing, Skydance issued approximately 3.918 billion non-voting Class B shares at $12 per share, generating $47.01 billion in gross proceeds.

Separately, Skydance filed a prospectus supplement on November 27 registering up to approximately 4.62 billion Class B shares for potential resale by certain stockholders. Shares issued to private-placement investors remain subject to transfer restrictions until April 4, 2027, with certain exceptions.

The registration does not mean those shares will necessarily be sold.

What Retail Think About SKYD Stock

As of this writing, SKYD stock was up nearly 2%. On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around the stock turned ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’ a day ago.

So far this year, SKYD stock has fallen over 49%. In comparison, the State Street Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLC), which holds the stock, has fallen more than 8% over the same period.

data.title: AAII investors leave the middle ground
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes rise; Nasdaq out front, up >1%
  • Consumer discretionary leads S&P 500 sector gainers; just healthcare edges red
  • STOXX 600 index up ~1%
  • Dollar, US crude gain; gold up >1.5%; bitcoin down >1.5%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~4.91%

AAII INVESTORS LEAVE THE MIDDLE GROUND

Individual investors grew more polarized in the latest American Association of Individual Investors (AAII) Sentiment Survey, with both bullish and bearish views rising as neutral sentiment continued to retreat.

Bearish sentiment, reflecting expectations that US stocks will fall over the next six months, climbed 3.2 percentage points to 45.4%. Pessimism remains unusually high and has now stayed above its historical average of 31.5% for a 42nd straight week.

Bullish sentiment, reflecting expectations that stocks will rise over the next six months, rose even more, gaining 3.8 percentage points to 37.1%. Optimism remained below its long-term average of 37.5% for a fifth time in six weeks, though it has improved recently.

The biggest move came from the middle ground. Neutral sentiment, which reflects expectations for little change in stock prices over the next six months, fell nearly 7 percentage points to 17.5%, remaining well below its historical average of 31.0% and marking a 38th consecutive week below that norm.

With neutral sentiment remaining unusually low, the shift suggests individual investors are increasingly taking a side on the market's outlook rather than expecting stocks to remain largely unchanged over the next six months.

As a result, the bull-bear spread narrowed slightly to negative 8.3% from negative 8.9% last week. While still firmly in negative territory and below its historical average of 6.5% for a 19th straight week, the modest improvement reflects bullish sentiment rising faster than bearish sentiment.

data.title: Besra Gold Inc Reminds Shareholders to Vote in Advance of Deadline for 2026 Annual Meeting of Shareholders
data.description:
Perth, Western Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Besra Gold Inc. ("Besra" or the "Company") reminds shareholders that its annual general and special meeting ("AGM") is scheduled to be held in Toronto on 7 December 2026. Participation by all shareholders is particularly important this year, as the AGM is being held in the context of sustained efforts by a group of minority shareholders to reconstitute the Company's board of directors (the "Board"). Your vote is crucial to support the incumbent members of the Board and the positive momentum that is building at Besra.

Since shareholders voted to reconstitute the Board at the special meeting held on 23 June 2025, a group of minority shareholders of the Company (the "Dissident Group") have repeatedly sought to replace or constrain the Board, including by attempting to requisition shareholder meetings on at least seven occasions, soliciting support from select shareholders without making public disclosure available to all shareholders, and most recently, purporting to nominate a slate of directors for election at the AGM. These efforts have repeatedly failed to comply with applicable law and the Company's constating documents. Throughout, the Company has engaged with members of the Dissident Group and encouraged them to pursue their objectives through proper legal channels available to shareholders. It is in this context that the Company will hold its fifth shareholder meeting in approximately two years.

Purported Director Nominations

On 6 November 2026, the Company received a notice from a member of the Dissident Group purporting to nominate four individuals for election at the AGM, two of whom have already been rejected by shareholders of the Company at past shareholder meetings:

(1) Mr David Potter, who briefly served as Chair of the Board from 19 May 2025 until he was removed by shareholders on 23 June 2025. Mr Potter was narrowly elected to the Board again on 15 December 2025, before again being removed by shareholders on 16 June 2026.

(2) Mr Matthew Antill, who previously served as managing director of a subsidiary of the Company, until being made redundant from that role effective 22 December 2025. Mr Antill recently stood for election at the meeting of shareholders held on 16 June 2026 and was not elected.

(3) Mr Brady Jausel, a member of the Dissident Group who has repeatedly sought to requisition shareholder meetings to replace the Board and is now proposed to join the Board himself.

(4) Ms Joanna Line-Jollymore, a Canadian elementary school teacher, who was added as a nominee after the Company advised the Dissident Group of the Canadian director requirements that apply to the Company.

The Board has reviewed the director nominations and has concluded that they were not made in compliance with the Company's advance notice by-law. Under the by-law, only persons nominated in accordance with its procedures are eligible for election as directors. The advance notice by-law is similar to by-laws adopted by many other Canadian public companies and is intended to ensure that shareholders are provided with relevant disclosure about persons proposed for election as directors.

The Company's legal counsel wrote to the nominating shareholder on 11 November 2026 setting out the deficiencies in its purported nominations. As of the date of this announcement, the Company has not received a response.

Lack of Disclosure to Shareholders

The nomination notice submitted to the Company lists fourteen individuals who are identified as joint actors in connection with the nominations, many of whom participated in the Dissident Group's previous attempts to replace the Board. Despite this private acknowledgement, the Dissident Group has made no public disclosure regarding its existence, its members, the extent of their interests in Besra, or their intentions for the Company should they succeed in replacing the Board. Instead, it has been brought to the Company's attention that members of the Dissident Group have contacted other shareholders of the Company directly to solicit their support.

The Company has significant concerns that the Dissident Group is effectively conducting a shadow proxy contest, privately seeking the support of select shareholders, rather than making public disclosure to all shareholders and seeking their support in accordance with applicable law and established procedures for shareholders seeking to reconstitute a board of directors. The Company has repeatedly encouraged members of the Dissident Group to obtain legal advice and to comply with applicable laws. These concerns have been brought to the attention of Canadian securities regulators.

Shareholders who are contacted by members of the Dissident Group or persons acting on their behalf are encouraged to exercise caution and to rely on the Company's public disclosure, which is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Message from the Chair

Commenting on the purported nominations, Besra Chairman Dr John Blake said:

"The Board recognises that voting at the Company's recent shareholder meetings reflects a range of sincerely held views regarding the future direction of Besra. Differences of opinion are not unusual in a public company, and the Board values engaged shareholders who care deeply about the future of Besra and the value of their investment. While shareholders may hold differing views on aspects of strategy, governance or execution, I believe all parties share a common objective: to maximise the long-term value of Besra's assets and position the Company for sustainable success."

"The latest nominations, however, continue a campaign of destabilisation that is counter to that objective. The current Board has worked tirelessly to address a number of significant legacy issues that have affected the Company and to establish a pathway to develop the Bau Gold Project in a manner that is responsible, sustainable, and that restores value for our shareholders. Tenure, feasibility, and funding are the cornerstones of responsible project development, and they must apply in the case of Bau. There are no shortcuts available. These objectives – tenure, feasibility and funding – have been a focus of the current Board, which believes that responsible governance is necessary to build the trust and confidence of stakeholders, including key decision makers in the Sarawak Government."

"What is important now is that Besra moves forward constructively in the best interests of all shareholders. Recurring campaigns of this kind that repeatedly propose leadership changes that shareholders have previously declined to endorse are a counterproductive diversion of resources and attention at a time when the Company and its Board need to focus on creating shareholder value. Following the AGM, we hope that all shareholders, including the members of the Dissident Group, will remain constructively engaged while supporting a period of stability that allows the Board to build on the Company's momentum in its next stages of growth. To that end, the Board unanimously encourages shareholders to vote FOR the re-election of each of the incumbent directors at the AGM."

Deadline to Vote

CDI holders must submit voting instruction forms no later than 9:00 a.m. (Perth, Australia time) on 2 December 2026 or no later than four full business days before any adjournment or postponement of the AGM. Proxies must be submitted by 9:00 a.m. (Perth, Australia time) on 4 December 2026 or no later than 48 hours prior to any adjournment or postponement of the AGM. For additional information regarding the AGM, shareholders are encouraged to review the Company's management information circular dated 20 October 2026, which is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

This announcement has been authorised for release by the Board of Besra Gold Inc.

data.title: Nvidia stock falls after premarket gains as volatile week nears its end
data.description:
Nvidia shares rose 4% before the opening bell of a shortened trading session Friday. But the gains are offering little evidence that the chipmaker had put a volatile week behind it.

The stock has swung sharply over the past three sessions, surging 31% on Monday after Jensen Huang's dramatic return as chief executive and president, only to give back some of those gains in the following sessions.

Nvidia fell 5.9% on Tuesday as investors took profits. Trading remained choppy ahead of the Thanksgiving break, with shares closing 3.91% lower on Wednesday after falling as much as 7% during the session.

The AI trade, with Nvidia at its center, has faced pressure from concerns over whether massive investments in AI will generate sufficient returns, a possible slowdown in spending after the U.S. midterm elections, and rising interest rates. Huang's departure had added another layer of uncertainty.

His return has removed that concern, at least for now. Huang's comeback added about $1T to Nvidia's market value and lifted the broader AI trade. But this has also introduced a key man risk in the company.
